Tor, "The Onion Router" is a great way to keep yourself anonymous by masking your IP with Tor exit nodes (Not all are safe, but you can get around this.) Today I will teach you not how to system level route, but program specific route through Tor (Not as "secure" but I use it.)

First install Tor. sudo apt-get install tor or your respected method. Yum etc.

Now sudo pkill tor

Now run Tor by typing tor into your terminal, what this will do is setup a localhost SOCKS5, which is what you'll use to route through Tor. Running Tor doesn't actually route anything.

Go to your preferred program, for this example I'll use the XChat IRC client and input these settings. Almost universal on any program. https://veuwer.com/i/2t7v.png You can use 9150 or 9050 as a port.

Make sure to use plugins if on Firefox like HTTPS Everywhere, uBlock, Flashblock, and WebRTC block.

Now, the most secure method is using a VM (I use to do this, but stopped due to performance issues. Doesn't apply to you.) VM's are really safe. Just follow https://www.whonix.org/wiki/Download#First_time_user.3F instructions. You don't have to do the security advice before/after part, but some of it's actually useful.
